title: Synthetic health sentinel and graceful backpressure coordinator for autoscaler stability
creator: Ravi Patel
description:
Summary:
We will implement a lightweight synthetic health sentinel and a graceful backpressure coordinator to stabilize autoscaling across regions and protect SLOs.

Background:
Recent incidents showed that noisy readiness signals and sudden autoscaler churn in overload windows cause multi-region failovers that significantly inflate tail latency and token cost. Current readiness checks depend heavily on short-lived probe windows and raw CPU metrics which amplify oscillations during traffic bursts.

Problem statement:
1) Readiness/liveness toggles are too sensitive to transient latency spikes from cold KV cache or model warming, causing premature pod evictions.
2) The autoscaler reacts to narrow-window signals and leads to thrashing across regions during global bursts.
3) Circuit-breaker fallbacks are binary today and lack a scoring mechanism to gracefully shed load while preserving high-priority tokens/SLOs.

Proposal (high level):
- Add a synthetic health sentinel that issues small, representative synthetic transactions (L0 requests) to exercise the full request path (runtime + model cache + network) at controlled cadence per node. Use a multi-factor score combining node liveness, median tail-latency of L0 transactions, and model KV-hit rate.
- Replace binary readiness flips with a graded readiness score exposed as a numeric signal to the autoscaler and region router. The autoscaler will use a smoothed EWMA of the readiness score plus tokenized CPU/latency signals to make scaling decisions.
- Implement a graceful backpressure coordinator that: 1) applies token-aware admission controls when region health degrades, 2) triggers soft circuit-breaker scoring that reduces low-priority requests first, and 3) integrates with routing policies to prefer healthier regions without triggering mass failover.

Design details:
- Sentinel cadence: default 1 L0 per pod per 30s, configurable by deployment. L0 payloads are small deterministic prompts that exercise model latency and cache.
- Health score composition: strings "liveness:1/0", "median_l0_ms", "kv_hit_rate_pct", "error_rate_1m_pct" -> normalized and aggregated into a 0-100 health score.
- Autoscaler integration: new metric "redwood.node_health_score" exported to the autoscaler stack. Autoscaler computes an EWMA over 60s with a 3s poll frequency to reduce sensitivity. Scaling decisions require sustained degradation for a 2-minute window before scale-down/scale-up actions.
- Backpressure policy: define priority classes (system, premium, best-effort). During health < 40 score, start shedding best-effort traffic in 10% increments every 15s until score recovers or minimum capacity is hit.
- Circuit-breaker scoring: transition from on/off to score-based thresholds (green >70, amber 40-70, red <40) with configurable hysteresis to avoid flip-flopping.

Telemetry and SLOs:
- New dashboards: per-region health score heatmap, L0 latency p95/p99, KV cache hit rate, admission rejections by priority class.
- SLO mapping: health score < 50 should correspond to routed fallback policies rather than abrupt region failover; ensure 99.9% of premium traffic meets latency SLO during controlled shed.

Testing and rollout:
- Unit tests for score computation and admission logic.
- Integration tests in staging with synthetic burst generator.
- Chaos tests: node restart, slow KV responses, and injected model cold-start latency to validate graceful degradation and autoscaler smoothing.
- Canary rollout: enable sentinel in a single region (us-west-2) for 24 hours with golden traffic, then 10% of pods cluster-wide, then full rollout.

Acceptance criteria:
1) No increase in pod churn attributable to readiness flips during 5x synthetic bursts in staging.
2) Autoscaler shows reduced scale-in/out frequency (target 40% lower oscillation) in controlled benchmarks.
3) Premium request p95 latency remains within SLO during controlled shedding tests.
4) Dashboards show clear health-score-to-routing actions correlation and fallbacks trigger at amber/red thresholds rather than binary failover.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Sentinel L0s add noise to capacity. Mitigation: very small L0s, adaptive cadence, and rate limits per node.
- Risk: Health score aggregation complexity leads to miscalibration. Mitigation: start with simple weights and expose tuning parameters; run A/B experiments.

Rollout tasks:
- Implement sentinel microclient and L0 payload set (CODE).
- Export health score metric and add to autoscaler policy engine (PR: github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/3482).
- Implement backpressure coordinator in routing plane and integrate with Console dashboards.
- Run staged chaos tests and benchmark (results documented in Confluence).
acceptance_criteria: No readiness-induced pod churn during 5x synthetic bursts in staging
Autoscaler oscillation frequency reduced by at least 40% in benchmark runs
Premium traffic p95 latency meets existing SLO during controlled shedding
Routing decisions reflect graded health scores and prevent mass region failover
